articles.title: Ethan Hawke blasts Hollywood's 'greedy bastards,' predicts massive rebellion against powerful elites
articles.summary: Ethan Hawke predicts massive rebellion in music and live theater against Hollywood's "greedy bastards" who he says control the entertainment industry.
articles.body: Ethan Hawke isn't holding back when it comes to the powerful forces he believes are controlling the entertainment industry. During a new interview with GQ, the Oscar-nominated actor took aim at wealthy power players, blasting "greedy bastards" who think they control every aspect of Hollywood and predicting a major rebellion against the industry. "I believe in rebellion. And I think people are going to wake up and punch back and there’s going to be massive movements in music and massive movements in live theater and massive movements of people getting together," Hawke said. FROM ‘SCREAM’ TO STREAM: JAMIE KENNEDY REVEALS HOW HOLLYWOOD LOST ITS WAY AND WHY HE WON'T GIVE UP ON LA "So don’t worry that the money and the greedy bastards that think they control everybody, they always lose in the end," he continued. "And they’re all going in the grave eventually. They think they’re winning, but they’re losing because their lives are worthless." Hawke also expressed frustration with the financial pressures shaping Hollywood, arguing that the projects actors care about most often come with the smallest paychecks. TRUMP, SCHIFF FORGE UNLIKELY ALLIANCE AS HOLLYWOOD BLEEDS JOBS "There's a direct correlation. I find that the more you love a project, the less you get paid," he said. "If you want to beat the algorithm, it's very difficult to do that and be paid." This isn't the first time Hawke has spoken about the pitfalls of Hollywood. ROBERT DOWNEY JR. SLAMS MODERN CELEBRITY CULTURE AS 'ABSOLUTE HORSES---' Last year, the actor called celebrity a "poison" for a young actor's brain. During an appearance on "The Joe Rogan Experience," Hawke got candid about his start in Hollywood as a young man and reflected on the psychological effect of becoming famous at a young age. "I think celebrity is like a tiny drop of mercury. Or it's poison. It's poison for your brain," the actor said. "To be a professional actor at a young age, it's dangerous in extremely insidious ways that are very, very hard to perceive when it's happening," Hawke said. Rogan compared the experience of becoming famous as a child to concrete. If concrete is made incorrectly, with the wrong amount of water or cement, that's it, he explained. Rogan added that once it dries there is no way to repair or fix it. DISNEY ALUM CHRISTY CARLSON ROMANO RIPS HOLLYWOOD FOR FAILING CHILD STARS AFTER HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S DEATH "That analogy works for all walks of life. Really. If you have something really traumatic happen in childhood, it's very hard to recover. It's a tremendous amount of work to recover. And I agree with you, like I think celebrity is like a tiny drop of mercury. Or it's a poison. It's a poison for your brain," Hawke said. During his GQ interview, Hawke expressed the same sentiment. "I wouldn’t be the first person to say that there’s an aspect of celebrity that is like a disease," he said. "And you can handle little bits of it, but too much of it — we can see what happened to Elvis and we can see Michael Jackson. It’s a form of isolation. It’s like being put in a zoo, and zoo animals go nuts. So do human beings." "And it seems like a kind of nice isolation because people are giving you money, and they’re telling you you’re wonderful, but nobody’s being real with you," he continued. "And that makes people insane. And they start scratching, trying to find some real life. And sometimes people do that with drugs, some people do that with acting out or getting in fights or whatever the ways that people do it." Last year, fellow actor Dakota Johnson also ripped into Hollywood, calling the industry an absolute "mess." During her appearance on the show "Hot Ones," Johnson was asked why "Hollywood is risk-averse." "I think it’s hard when creative decisions are made by a committee, and it’s hard when creative decisions are made by people who don’t even really watch movies or know anything about them … that tends to be what’s occurring a lot," Johnson shared with host Sean Evans. Johnson, who has grown up in the business as the daughter of actors Melanie Griffith and Don Johnson, is no stranger to the inner workings of Hollywood. The "Fifty Shades of Grey" actress’ comments come as studios continue to create sequels and remakes, with original storytelling often sidelined. "When something does well … studios want to keep that going so they remake the same things," she claimed. "But humans don’t want that. They want fresh. They want to feel new things, experience new things, see new things." She added, "So I don’t know, I guess it’s all just a bit of a mess right now, isn’t it?" articles.title: Selma Blair's on-off boyfriend asks fans to 'pray' for actress after Delta flight incident, assault charges
articles.summary: Selma Blair's on-off boyfriend Andy Kiernan asked fans to "pray for Selma" as the actress faced assault charges following an alleged Delta flight incident at JFK.
articles.body: Selma Blair's on-again, off-again boyfriend pleaded for compassion after the actress' arrest and subsequent assault charges following an alleged mid-air incident aboard a Delta flight to New York. Andy Kiernan asked social media followers to "pray for Selma," in an Instagram story shared Monday. "She has a good heart," he wrote. "She hasn't yet got the help she needs. Pray that she does." SELMA BLAIR ARRESTED AFTER IN-FLIGHT INCIDENT He added, "She's a human being like the rest of us. Pray for Arthur too." Kiernan was referring to Blair's 15-year-old son, Arthur Saint Bleick, who she co-parents with fashion designer Jason Bleick. SELMA BLAIR ACCUSED OF KICKING NURSE HOURS AFTER JFK PLANE ARREST It's unclear when the pair began dating and if they're currently in a relationship. The actress went public with Kiernan in 2024, according to photos published by the Daily Mail. Kiernan and Blair's representatives did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Blair, 54, was arraigned Monday on two counts of second-degree assault stemming from alleged attacks on a Port Authority police officer and a nurse following her arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport from Los Angeles. Police had responded to a call about a "physically abusive passenger" aboard Delta Flight 938. SELMA BLAIR SAYS ‘NO ONE RETURNED MY CALLS’ AFTER ANTI-ISLAM COMMENT LED TO HOLLYWOOD FALLOUT Judge Indira Khan set bail at $20,000 cash/$60,000 bond/$60,000 partially secured bond. She's expected in court in January 2027. The "Hellboy" actress was taken into custody at JFK and transported to a hospital for evaluation following the in-flight incident. Two flight attendants reported injuries, and one was taken to a hospital, according to officials. Police officer Maria Suarez was helping secure Blair on a stretcher at approximately 11:50 p.m. ET when Blair allegedly "removed her leg from the stretcher straps and kicked Officer Suarez repeatedly about the face, neck and chest," according to an affidavit. Suarez suffered swelling to her jaw and "substantial pain to her face, neck and chest," and was then treated at a Queens-area hospital, according to the filing. Blair is also accused of kicking a nurse in the chest at a Queens hospital. "This was not an intentional assault," the outlet noted that her attorney, Shawn Barnes, said in court. "Ms. Blair missed several doses of … a powerful medication that controls severe neurological symptoms. "Ms. Blair boarded this flight after being on set and working extensive hours and exhaustive hours in the days leading up to this flight." He added, "Additionally, at one point, during the flight, there was an incident where Miss Blair actually fell and hit her head. articles.title: Hollywood star sounds alarm over disappearing jobs as productions flee California
articles.summary: Hollywood’s ongoing production exodus is leaving actors and crew members struggling to find work, as Jeff Garlin and Bryan Callen describe the industry’s declining opportunities.
articles.body: When Adam Carolla asked actor and comedian Jeff Garlin on his podcast last week whether there was "anything going on in Hollywood anymore," the "Curb Your Enthusiasm" star admitted that acting roles had virtually dried up for him. "I haven't worked in almost three years since ‘Curb’ ended," Garlin said, prefacing his remarks with uncertainty about whether he should reveal his circumstances. "…The reason that you and I do this no longer exists. It doesn’t." "We could be doing this thing in Sweden," he added. HOLLYWOOD JOBS FLEE OVERSEAS AS CONGRESS SCRAMBLES TO STOP PRODUCTION EXODUS — WITH TRUMP'S BLESSING With that comment, Garlin was referring to the growing number of productions that have left not only California but the country altogether. Meanwhile, California Gov. Gavin Newsom's office said last week that a new post-production tax credit, an expanded film and television tax credit, and protections for actors against AI-generated content are expected to help Hollywood. In total, 35 films, 28 of which are independent projects, received production incentives in the latest round of awards under the California Film Commission's expanded Film and Television Tax Credit Program. The commission estimates the projects will generate more than $1 billion in direct production spending, create jobs for more than 5,400 cast and crew members, and employ 24,800 background actors. HOLLYWOOD FEELING MORE HOPEFUL AMID A PUSH FOR FILM TAX CREDITS AND PARAMOUNT STAYING PUT, FILMMAKER SAYS Additionally, a bipartisan coalition of lawmakers is working on a federal tax credit for film and television productions that could be used alongside state production incentives. Even with the proposed and expanded incentives, conversations with people in Hollywood suggest that uncertainty remains about whether the measures will bring production jobs back. NEWSOM SAYS FILM TAX INCENTIVES ARE BRINGING HOLLYWOOD HOME BUT INDUSTRY EXPERTS WARN IT MAY BE 'TOO LATE' "The number of American productions that are filmed in Ireland tells you all you need to know. All these empty sound stages. It's a shame," Garlin said. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the industry has lost 49,000 jobs since 2022, following the COVID-19 pandemic and a slowdown in streaming production. TRUMP, SCHIFF FORGE UNLIKELY ALLIANCE AS HOLLYWOOD BLEEDS JOBS TRUMP CALLS HOLLYWOOD A 'TOTAL DISASTER,' PUSHES FEDERAL TAX INCENTIVE FOR FILM AFTER MEETING WITH JON VOIGHT Actor and comedian Bryan Callen told Fox News Digital that he sympathizes with Garlin but wasn't surprised by his admission. "You can’t make your living as just an actor anymore in Los Angeles. If you do a series on, say, Netflix, and it's a 10-episode series, do the math. Take a look at what’s left after taxes and commissions to your manager, your agent, whoever it might be," Callen said, emphasizing the high cost of producing films and television shows in Los Angeles. CHRIS ROCK EXPOSES BRUTAL REALITY OF HOLLYWOOD AFTER DECADES OF FAME "You are living, if you are lucky, a middle-class existence, but probably lower than that when you take into account how expensive everything is in Los Angeles — property and just having to live and buy food and all that stuff," he said. Callen himself has increasingly turned to stand-up comedy and podcasting rather than relying solely on acting. "I was like, I can't put all my eggs in this acting basket," he said, pointing to several factors that have diminished the cultural prominence of Hollywood’s biggest movie stars. "This business has been so atomized. The days of all of us going to one place, whether it's a TV show or a movie, to watch that one person are long gone… And if that's the case, big names are no longer big names. They just aren't." Still, despite what Callen described as the demise of Hollywood’s "monoculture" — an era when major stars alone could draw audiences to television shows and movies — he doesn’t believe Hollywood itself is going away. "Remember this about Los Angeles," Callen said. "First of all, you shot there because the weather was predictable. It wasn't going to rain you out. And number two, the best of the best still lives in Los Angeles." "People think they can move this business to Texas or whatever. No, you can't. At the end of the day, you still have the best sound engineers, the best directors, the best writers, the best special effects people, the best people who score film and all that." While Carolla and Garlin may share Callen’s perspective on Hollywood’s enduring strengths, they still had plenty to lament about the current state of the entertainment business in the Golden State. "I talked to a friend of mine… He's been working as an editor nonstop for 32 years…," Carolla said. "And he goes, ‘I'm retired. There's no work.’" "Everyone is moving out, and it’s affecting — I mean, again, everyone thinks about the actor, the director, but a crew has so many people that work, hairdressers, catering, craft service people, crew members." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I moved here to be in a world where Bob Newhart and Mel Brooks opened the doors, and you followed through," Garlin said. "It used to be, ‘Boy, you’re lucky, even if you’re talented, to break through.’ Now, it’s, ‘You’re lucky if someone even notices you’re in the room.’"

articles.title: Netflix despedirá al 6% de su plantilla global: su mayor ronda de despidos desde el año 2022
articles.standfirst: El gigante del streaming y el entretenimiento prescindirá de 1.000 puestos de trabajo
articles.summary: El gigante del streaming y el entretenimiento prescindirá de 1.000 puestos de trabajo
articles.body: Netflix tendrá que despedir al 6% de su plantilla global, es decir, unos 1.000 puestos de trabajo. Será su mayor ronda de despidos desde el año 2022. De todo ello, informaron este miércoles, 14 de octubre, medios estadounidenses como The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) y la cadena CNBC, tal y como apuntó la agencia EFE. Esta medida que plantea el gigante del streaming afectará a los departamentos de producto, tecnología, asuntos legales y recursos humanos. Esto sucede en un marco de desaceleración del crecimiento y preocupación por la evolución de la interacción de los usuarios con la plataforma. Ted Sarandos y Greg Peters, codirectores ejecutivos de Netflix, justificaron, según informan los mencionados rotativos, esta decisión por la necesidad de priorizar recursos. “Nuestra misión de entretener al mundo es ambiciosa, y cumplirla exige que seamos disciplinados sobre dónde priorizamos a nuestra gente y nuestros recursos”. Pese a estos despidos, desde las altas esferas de la compañía afirman que todo lo que rodea a Netflix “sigue fuerte” y en el plano económico cumplirán sus “previsiones financieras”. Además, seguirán invirtiendo de “manera agresiva” en áreas de alto impacto. Cabe recalcar que esta decisión llega justo antes de que Netflix presente sus resultados financieros del último trimestre el próximo 20 de octubre. Además, a finales de 2025, la compañía informó que tenía 16.000 empleados a tiempo completo, por lo que ahora serán 1.000 menos que por aquel entonces. No es la única compañía del sector que ha optado por dar este paso recientemente: Disney y Amazon han acometido recortes de personal en los últimos años. Por último, esta noticia llega tan solo un día después de conocerse que la plataforma de streaming había llegado a un acuerdo para los derechos del Mundial 2030 y emitirlo de manera exclusiva al completo en nuestro país y en Andorra.

articles.title: Heavy traffic expected on Pune-Mumbai Expressway, old highway; police urge use of public transport
articles.summary: Pune-Mumbai Expressway, old highway to see heavy traffic till Tuesday; police urge public transport. Heavy vehicle restrictions and diversions in place till Oct 20.
articles.body: PUNE: Traffic police have requested people to use public transport as much as possible with heavy vehicular rush being expected on both Pune-Mumbai expressway and the old highway this weekend through Tuesday.The district administration has already ordered the diversion of heavy and large vehicles from the old highway to alternative routes from Thursday to prevent congestion during Shri Ekvira Devi Navratri festival. Highway police have also increased patrolling on the expressway to ensure that heavy vehicles do not occupy the first two lanes.The order issued by the collector on Tuesday under Section 115 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, prohibits entry of heavy and large vehicles round the clock on the stretch between Karla Phata and the foothill temple of Shri Ekvira Devi until Oct 20.It further says that from Oct 15 to 19, heavy and large vehicles will not be allowed on the old Mumbai-Pune highway between Kusgaon Budruk toll plaza in Lonavla and Vadgaon Phata in Vadgaon Maval, from 6 am to 10 pm. Vehicle operators have been advised to use Mumbai-Pune expressway via Urse toll plaza as an alternative route.With Dasara on Tuesday being a holiday, people who are planning to take off from work on Monday, or take the work-from-home option, may have an extended weekend holiday. Vijay Pandey, a businessman living in Borivali, Mumbai, said, “I am travelling to Pune to visit my friends. I usually drive. But this time, I and my partner are planning to book Vande Bharat to travel. We don’t want to get stuck on the highway,” he said.Shivaji Pawar, superintendent of police (SP), Highway Traffic Police, Pune range, said heavy vehicles travelling to and from Chakan and Talegaon to Mumbai will be diverted to the expressway, due to which the vehicular movement on the Mumbai-Lonavala stretch of the expressway is expected to increase.“We have already had a discussion with Pune Rural Police regarding traffic management. We will engage 50 of our total strength of 60 on ground during the weekend. Moreover, rural police station personnel will also be in full force managing the traffic. We are hoping that more people will travel via railways and use public transport during these days as pilgrims are expected to come in large numbers, especially during the weekend and towards the last days of Navaratra till Tuesday. We urge people to restrain from travelling if avoidable during the heavy rush days,” said Pawar, adding that they have been imposing fines on heavy vehicles that do not follow lane discipline.As per the collector’s order, the heavy vehicles travelling towards Pune on the old Mumbai-Pune highway will be diverted via Kusgaon Budruk toll plaza in Lonavala onto the Expressway and towards Pune city through Urse toll plaza. Similarly, heavy vehicles travelling towards Mumbai will be diverted from Talegaon Phata in Vadgaon through Urse Ghat and onto Mumbai-Pune expressway. articles.title: Sally Rooney’s Books Pulled From U.K. Shelves Amid Controversy Over Palestine Action Support
articles.summary: “I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences,” the 'Normal Peo...
articles.body:
Normal People author Sally Rooney has shared that her books will no longer be available for sale in the U.K. because of her support for protest group Palestine Action .

Given that the British government has outlawed Palestine Action as a terrorist organization, Rooney's publisher Faber confirmed to the Associated Press that it "has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on U.K. earnings to Sally Rooney for her work."

In a statement Faber said, "To sell a writer's work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher. As such, and in full agreement with Sally, we have taken the decision that we can no longer supply her works in the U.K. in any format."

Faber's decision to withdraw her books from sale in the U.K. was made "with my full agreement," Rooney says.

"I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences," Rooney said in a statement, according to the AP. Proceeds from her novels and TV fees would be used to continue to support the group, Rooney shared.

The decision follows the author writing a column in The Irish Times last August titled, "Sally Rooney: I support Palestine Action. If this makes me a 'supporter of terror' under UK law, so be it."

The U.K. government banned the Palestine Action group after activists broke into a Royal Air Force base last June to protest British military support for Israel's military offensive against Hamas in Gaza.

In February, Britain's High Court ruled that the government's decision to outlaw the protest group was unlawful. The ban was kept in place pending another hearing to overturn it.

Among her work, Rooney has penned best-sellers Conversations With Friends and Normal People, both of which were adapted for limited television series. Normal People starred Daisy Edgar-Jones and Paul Mescal, while the cast of Conversations With Friends included Alison Oliver, Joe Alwyn, Sasha Lane and Jemima Kirke.

Rooney's additional published works include Beautiful World, Where Are You and Intermezzo .

articles.title: It’s doll coming back to me now: Celine Dion gets her own Barbie
articles.summary: Celine Dion is being made into a Barbie doll, one that will be sought by fans near, far, wherever they are.
articles.body: Celine Dion is being made into a doll, one that will be sought by fans near, far, wherever they are. The maker of Barbie announced it was releasing a special edition doll of Dion, 58, as part of its Mattel Creations line. The toy is modeled after the Canadian singer’s 1998 Oscars performance, where she sang “My Heart Will Go On” from James Cameron’s “Titanic” film. Dion’s doll form has the same hair style, long-sleeved gown from her performance, as well as the Heart of the Ocean, the necklace that was famously featured in the movie. The company announced the doll in an Instagram post and urged consumers not to wait. The caption noted that “she’s limited and she’s legendary.” The doll is the latest celebration of the 58-year-old’s career after Dion revealed she’d been diagnosed with a rare neurological disorder. She announced in 2022 that she had stiff-person syndrome, telling fans in a video that the disease was causing painful spasms that it made it difficult for her to walk. “Unfortunately, these spasms affect every aspect of my daily life, sometimes causing difficulties when I walk and not allowing me to use my vocal chords to sing the way I’m used to,” Dion said at the time. But Dion refused to allow the disease to stop her from singing. In 2024, she performed at the top of the Eiffel Tower in Paris for the Summer Olympics opening ceremony with her rendition of French singer Édith Piaf’s iconic “Hymne à l’amour.” Fans around the world were moved to see the singer triumph over her medical condition. Singer Kelly Clarkson, who was serving as a co-host for NBC’s broadcast, struggled to find the words that could describe the emotion of the scene. “If you know anything just about Celine right now ... this is her purpose. And if you know anything about what she’s going through right now and — I’m so sorry, I’m trying to hold it together — but that she got through that, that was incredible,” Clarkson said at the time, calling her a “gold winner for vocal athletes.” Dion returned to the stage again last month in a series of comeback concerts. It was the first of a 26-show residency in Paris where Dion gave fans a taste of some of her greatest hits. Among the songs chosen for the setlist was “All by Myself,” one of the most difficult vocal performances in Dion’s extensive catalogue of ballads. One American fan described the show to NBC News as a “victory lap.” “I think her belief is renewed, I think her spirit is renewed,” said Francesca Pezzulo.

articles.title: Hilary Swank, 52, Is Pregnant! Actress Expecting Third Baby 3 Years After Welcoming Twins
articles.summary: The actress and husband Philip Schneider are already parents to 3-year-old twins Aya and Ohm
articles.body:
Swank announced her pregnancy news with a video teasing that her "newest project" will arrive in December

The actress and her husband Philip Schneider welcomed twins Aya and Ohm in April 2023

Swank has said becoming a parent later in life gave her more patience and flexibility

The Yellowjackets actress, 52, is expecting her third baby with her husband Philip Schneider. Swank shared the exciting news with an adorable and creative video on Instagram .

In the clip, Swank's family dances with the lights off with glow sticks taped to their bodies. As her husband and twins dance, Swank appears with a baby bump featuring a tiny glow stick-clad baby.

"A lot of people have been asking what project I'm doing next, this one releases in December. 😉👼🏼🫶🏼," she captioned the video, hinting that she is due this winter.

Swank first became a mother when she welcomed her twins Aya and Ohm in April 2023.

While chatting with PEOPLE about her lobbying efforts for the California Bill AB 1901 , which calls for more transparency in diaper ingredients, the Million Dollar Baby actress shared she enjoyed her Mother's Day surrounded by family and that she's in a "really blessed position" to be able to spend time with her kids how she wants to.

Swank shared that it "just worked out" having her kids later in life because she can "be so present" with them.

"It just worked out that I had babies this much later in life," she said. "It wasn't that I didn't want them earlier. There were a lot of things that kept that from happening, and so I can really take time to be with them."

She added, "I feel like I get a lot of Mother's Days other than actual Mother's Day because of being able to be so present with them."

Reflecting on her decision to have her children later in life, the actress shared that she was much more career-driven in her earlier years, saying it didn't leave much room to tend to other things in life. She added that her acting career was "such a baby of mine" that ultimately she gave all of herself to developing her craft.

"I knew I wanted kids someday, but I wasn't planning what that would look like," she told PEOPLE. "I know it's so different for everyone, but for me, if I had had a kid in my 20s or my 30s, I think I'd be a much different parent than I am now."

"I feel like I have that more kind of ability to really give them my attention in a way that I wouldn't have as much at that point because it would've been pulled between the two in a very distinct way," continued Swank. "In my career being so established, I have the ability to kind of step in and step out when I choose, and that is just such a blessing."

Swank said she "couldn't have planned it" to work out the way it did, but she's grateful for the space she's in. The Away star explained that as an older mom, she has "much more patience and bandwidth" to raise her kids, adding other reasons why having kids later in life made her the best parent she could be for her twins.

"I've done a lot of work on myself," she added. "One of the things that I feel is important about being your best parenting self is having done that work, so you break any cycles that you don't want to impart on your children, and I've done a lot of that work over time, so I didn't have to do a lot of catch up with that."

Swank, who mostly keeps her little ones out of the public eye, said that she still has work to do within herself. However, Swank emphasized that she's more equipped to handle whatever comes her way.

"I still do my work. Don't get me wrong," she said. "I'm certainly not a perfect human being. But, I have the tools in which to deal with those things at hand rather than having to go search for them while I'm in the middle of it."

Swank told PEOPLE she is consistently learning how to "be in the moment" from her children, noting it's not an easy task.

"One of the things that I've always tried and aimed for as a goal is to be in the moment, and it's much harder than one would think," she said. "My kids have really taught me [that]."

"First of all, there's no one more in the moment than them, right?" she added. "They're just that perfect reminder of that, and that I don't want to lose sight of that."

articles.title: Matthew McConaughey, 56, worth $200 million, spent two days in a West Texas desert reading 20 years of bad reviews; Oscar winner reveals how he separated hate from constructive criticism
articles.summary: Matthew McConaughey has an Oscar, an estimated net worth of $200 million and a career spanning more than three decades.
articles.body: Matthew McConaughey has an Oscar, an estimated net worth of $200 million and a career spanning more than three decades. But despite his success in Hollywood, the actor once decided to confront some of the harshest criticism he had received throughout his career. He collected two decades' worth of negative reviews in a thick book, took it to the West Texas desert and spent two days reading them.The unusual exercise, which took place around 2018 or 2019 while he was writing his memoir Greenlights, helped McConaughey understand an important distinction: some criticism stems from personal dislike, while other feedback can offer valuable lessons about one's work.Speaking on the October 13 episode of the Build or Break podcast, hosted by Kind snack food brand founder Daniel Lubetzky, the 56-year-old actor opened up about the emotionally challenging experience and explained how it changed his approach to criticism.Matthew McConaughey spent two days reading his worst reviewsDuring the conversation, Lubetzky asked McConaughey how he ensures that criticism of his acting performances does not affect his self-worth. The actor responded by recalling how he once gathered 20 years of negative reviews and immersed himself in them.McConaughey joked that he believed the critics who had written positive reviews were the intelligent ones before explaining the exercise.“I read every one. All the negative reviews — I’m sorry, not all the positive reviews, the negative ones,” he said. “And I sat, and it’s all I [did], I spent two days with them. It was hard.”The actor explained that reading the reviews together allowed him to recognise the difference between criticism motivated by personal animosity and feedback that genuinely assessed his performances.“Some of the reviews, what I learned, is that from the very first sentence, ‘Oh, this person has it out for me.’ It didn’t matter whether they saw the movie or not. They just don’t like me. They were going to write a negative review,” he said.'This person’s got a point'Not every negative review, however, was something McConaughey could dismiss. Some critics, he realised, understood his work but felt that his performances had not achieved what he intended.“Other reviews I saw, I was like, ‘This person’s got a point. They’re actually a fan of mine, and they didn’t get from my performance what I was actually hoping they would have got. Where did I fail in the choice?’ Because this is constructive criticism,” he explained.He added that such reviews helped him identify areas where he could have performed better.“This person is a good critic. They were looking at the work and objectively criticizing it. Applauding some things, but also applauded some things that shined a light on where I came up short. Okay. What can I learn from that?” McConaughey said.The actor's takeaway was that criticism should not automatically be accepted or rejected. Instead, it is important to determine whether the person is genuinely evaluating the work and offering something useful.“Some are going to write bad about you and wish you the worst no matter what, because they just don’t like you from afar and don’t like your success, what have you,” he said. “Some are really a good critic who will write constructively about what you did wrong, and you can learn from it.”Matthew McConaughey on the difference between acting success and personal validationMcConaughey has been acting on screen since 1993, when he made his feature film debut in Dazed and Confused. His filmography includes projects such as A Time to Kill, Contact, How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days, The Lincoln Lawyer and Interstellar.Over the years, he has also spoken about deliberately stepping away from romantic comedies to pursue more dramatic roles. In the late 2000s, he took a 20-month hiatus from acting as part of a career shift that eventually became associated with the period known as the “McConaissance”.During the podcast conversation, the actor reflected on how fame changed the way people responded to him. Before becoming a Hollywood star, he said, praise and affection were more directly connected to how he performed his job and conducted himself.“Before I became a ‘movie star’ or ‘celebrity,’ everything that I had done in life or was measured upon or got a hug for or was told ‘I love you’ for or was told ‘Hey, you did that wrong,’ was measured off of how I did the job,” he said.However, he found that success in Hollywood could bring a sudden flood of admiration that was not necessarily connected to the quality of his work.“And Hollywood, a successful weekend, all of a sudden these people ‘I love you, I love you, I love you,’ and champagne coming,” he recalled.McConaughey continued, “I’m like, ‘Wait a minute, what’s your name again?’ I’ve only said ‘I love you’ to four people in my life and all of a sudden everyone is saying it. Wow, this place is great, or is this place kind of heat-seeking?”His experience helped him recognise how difficult it can be to distinguish genuine feedback from the reactions that come with celebrity and commercial success.What is Matthew McConaughey working on now?McConaughey most recently appeared on the big screen in The Rivals of Amziah King, released in August, marking his return to theatrical releases after his last such appearance in 2019.He is also set to appear alongside close friend Woody Harrelson in Brothers, an Apple TV series featuring dramatized versions of the two actors as themselves.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. The shop also said another singing bird automaton, priced at approximately $2,000, was available.The new price tag has added another layer to the public disagreement, which began after Clarkson visited the Brooklyn store over the weekend.How the dispute between Kelly Clarkson and Art of Play beganClarkson took to social media after her visit to Art of Play, saying she had travelled to Brooklyn to browse the shop and had several items in mind to purchase. You're an idiot and just lost a huge sale," she added.The singer later doubled down on her account after Art of Play disputed her version of events. Clarkson maintained that she had pointed to a $15,000 price tag and had been told the bird was available for purchase, only for an employee to suggest a comparable alternative."So you're not only rude, you're also a liar. Got it," she wrote in a follow-up post.Art of Play, however, has maintained that the encounter was a misunderstanding. The shop said Molly was a permanent fixture and that employees had offered Clarkson the option of purchasing a similar automaton directly from its creator.Shop owner says he came to work despite recovering from cancer removalFor Rubin, the controversy has become more personal than a disagreement over an unusual piece of merchandise. During his conversation with Fox News Digital, the co-owner revealed that he had recently undergone a medical procedure and was still recovering."I'm not even supposed to be here today. I got a cancer removed from my face last week," Rubin said."I'm getting the stitches out tonight," he added.Rubin said concerns about the shop's safety were the reason he came in despite being advised not to work while recovering. articles.title: John Stamos says Beach Boys legend Mike Love is facing 'serious health challenges'
articles.summary: John Stamos revealed Mike Love is facing serious health challenges, but the Beach Boys legend insisted on performing at the Ryman over the weekend.
articles.body: John Stamos performed with the Beach Boys on Sunday at the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville. Before the show, the actor was overcome with emotion talking about Beach Boys legend Mike Love, who is facing "serious health challenges." Stamos, 63, shared a carousel of images on social media with his "musical hero and mentor" before admitting he was "struggling" to put his feelings into words. ROD STEWART CONFIRMS FINAL TOUR AFTER HEART PROCEDURE AND HEALTH SCARES "My beloved friend, father figure, musical hero and mentor, Mike Love, is facing serious health challenges," he wrote. "We hope he’ll be doing what he loves for years to come, but we don’t know what the future holds. We have tonight." At Tuesday's Hot Cuisine fundraiser for the Scleroderma Research Foundation (SRF), Stamos told Fox News Digital it was his mission to get Love to the Ryman Auditorium for a performance of a lifetime. "Our goal was to get him up at the Ryman this weekend. He wanted it," Stamos said. "I've been spending a lot of time with him, you know, quiet time. We've been listening to music. … Doo-wop. He loves Doo-Wop. "And I said, ‘You gotta tell me, do you really think you can do these shows this weekend?’ He said, ‘Yes, and I really want to.’ I said, 'We'll make it happen.' "Everybody told him not to — doctors, his family — but it was something he wanted to do. He's made all my dreams come true and all my wishes. So, I had to fulfill his wish, and we made sure that he got there and did a good job." SRF presented John Stamos with the Bob Saget Legacy Award, recognizing his steadfast support for scleroderma research and his commitment to following in Bob’s footsteps by shining a spotlight on scleroderma and raising funds toward a cure. Love's representatives did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. It's unclear what health struggles Love faces. Stamos and Love's son, Brian Love, delivered speeches prior to the show. "One thing about him is he's stubborn, and he's steadfast, and he did not want to miss the Ryman. I mean, for good reason," Brian said, via Variety. "Look at this place. So, we are happy. We're going to be positive. We're gonna sing along. But I still remember something he told me when I was a child, and it stuck with me. I said, ‘Dad, why do you do so many shows?’ I mean, we are talking about a guy who's done over 100 concerts a year well up into his 80s." "That's just incredible, right? So, he told me, ‘Well, if you don’t do as many concerts, you don't see as many towns, and then that means less people get to hear the amazing Beach Boys personally.' So, he's always cared for the small towns, the fairs. … This is obviously a much more well-known, beautiful venue. But he cares about the listener, and I think it's such an honor to be part of that. And we've gotta live in the moment." Stamos said, "All we have is tonight really, and I think it's going to be very, very special. Mike, he insisted on being here. … He's done over 7,000 live shows. And tonight'll be 7,422, I think exactly. I think that's where we're at. He's counting. … We love you, and have the greatest night ever, and God bless you all." After the curtains opened, Love was already seated on stage, the outlet reported. He sang in his seat along with his bandmates but did not do his lead vocals. During the performance, the Beach Boys legend addressed concerns about his health, saying, "Obviously, I’ve been going through some health issues for quite a while. But I didn’t want to miss being at the Ryman with y’all." Variety reported that Love was helped up by Brian and Stamos at the end of the show as the song "We Are The Champions" by Queen played. JON BON JOVI ABRUPTLY ENDS MADISON SQUARE GARDEN SHOW AFTER HEALTH SETBACK In his social media post, Stamos acknowledged that Love "is a fighter," and despite "doctors, family and friends urging him to focus on his health, he insists on being on stage." "He says he needs his band, the audience, his friends and drummer surrounding him to lift him up," Stamos wrote. "I’ve played with Mike for 41 years. I never imagined how deeply it would affect me to see someone larger than life face something so human and fragile." The Beach Boys have been touring in support of the 60th anniversary of their groundbreaking 11th studio album, "Pet Sounds." Stamos noted that "the Mike Love we see tonight may not be exactly the Mike we’ve always known. But he’s still every bit the Mike we love." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "What he’s given me personally is immeasurable. "Forty-one years of stages, airplanes, hotel rooms, laughter and moments nobody else saw. He married Caitlin and me. He’s shared experiences with my family, and now my son." The "Full House" star noted that Love didn't only give him a spot in the band. He "gave me a place in his life." I carry those lessons everywhere," Stamos said. "He’s made me a better musician, entertainer and man. "This life with Mike and the Beach Boys has become part of my identity. I’ve felt entrusted with being a steward of this extraordinary music, carrying it to new generations." Stamos wanted to "be completely present" performing with Love at the Ryman over the weekend and "hear every harmony, familiar joke and cheer. Feel that first chord hit and watch age, illness and time disappear. Just a bunch of guys making music together." articles.summary: Compositor e violonista se apresenta como cantor no disco que lançará em 30 de outubro e que também traz Chico Buarque, Mônica Salmaso e Tom Veloso.
articles.body:
Cézar Mendes canta cinco das 12 músicas compostas com Arnaldo Antunes e reunidas no álbum 'Itapuano' — Foto: Bob Wolfenson / Divulgação

♬ Compositor e violonista baiano nascido em Santo Amaro da Purificação (BA) e revelado em 1998 como parceiro do conterrâneo Caetano Veloso em “Aquele frevo axé”, música que batizou álbum de Gal Costa (1945 – 2022), Cézar Mendes incursiona pela arte do canto em cinco das 12 músicas do segundo álbum do artista, “Itapuano”, programado para 30 de outubro.

Contudo, Mendes – que entrou em cena como cantor em fevereiro de 2024, mês em que fez o primeiro show em Salvador (BA) – não abre mão das participações estelares, tal como no primeiro álbum, “Depois enfim”, lançado em 2018 com elenco de convidados que incluía Adriana Calcanhotto, Arnaldo Antunes, Caetano Veloso, Djavan, Fernanda Montenegro, Marisa Monte, Moreno Veloso e Tom Veloso.

Aliás e a propósito, Calcanhotto, Caetano, Marisa, Moreno e Tom são nomes presentes ao longo das 12 faixas de “Itapuano”, álbum anunciado em 25 de setembro pelo single “João” .

A esse time, se juntam Alice Caymmi, Antonio Zambujo, Chico Buarque, Mônica Salmaso, Pedro Miranda e Sophie Charlotte, além de Mario Adnet, produtor e arranjador do álbum gravado entre agosto de 2025 e março deste ano de 2026 no Estúdio Sarapuí, na cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ).

O repertório do álbum “Itapuano” é calcado na parceria de Mendes com Arnaldo Antunes, iniciada há 22 anos com a gravação por Arnaldo da canção “Itapuana” no álbum “Saiba” (2004) – música ora revivida por Cézar Mendes em feat com Mônica Salmaso.

Entre regravações de “Enquanto passa outro verão” (2021), “O culpado é o cupido” (2023) e “Também pede bis” (2018), recicladas no álbum “Itapuano” com as vozes de Sophie Charlotte, Adriana Calcanhotto e Chico Buarque, respectivamente, Cézar Mendes apresenta músicas inéditas em disco como “Apenas milagre”, “Colibri” (composição que também tem a assinatura de Mario Adnet) e “Papel de bobo”, esta gravada com a voz de Alice Caymmi.

articles.title: Canadian singer Joni Mitchell officially becomes American citizen after 62-year journey
articles.summary: Joni Mitchell shared a photo and video from her naturalization ceremony, becoming a U.S. citizen at 82 while retaining Canadian citizenship.
articles.body: Joni Mitchell has officially become an American citizen at age 82, more than six decades after she first moved to the United States. The music icon, who hails from Canada, announced the news on Instagram, sharing a photo of herself beaming while holding an American flag along with a video from her naturalization ceremony. "A journey that began 62 years ago," Mitchell wrote in the caption of her post. ART GARFUNKEL JOINS GROWING LIST OF CELEBRITIES CONSIDERING A MOVE ABROAD OVER TRUMP PRESIDENCY Mitchell wore a red and navy blue floral cardigan that had an American flag pin along with a red beaded necklace, a red beret and black pants with black boots while posing in between an American flag and a Department of Homeland Security flag. In the video Mitchell uploaded, she was seated in the front row at the ceremony as the speaker announced, "And Joni Mitchell, Canada" to cheers and applause from the audience. According to KSL, Mitchell will also retain her Canadian citizenship because the U.S. and Canada legally permit dual citizenship. The legendary singer-songwriter was born Roberta Joan Anderson in Fort Macleod, Alberta, to Royal Canadian Air Force flight Lt. William Andrew Anderson and teacher Myrtle Marguerite. Mitchell's family lived on several bases during World War II before eventually settling in Saskatoon, which the singer has often referred to as her hometown. She went on to attend the Alberta College of Art in Calgary before dropping out and relocating to Toronto, where she played gigs at coffee houses and folk clubs. The "Both Sides Now" songstress moved to the United States in 1965 at age 21 after marrying American folk singer Chuck Mitchell. The former couple, who lived in Detroit, Michigan, performed together as a folk duo before divorcing in 1967. After their divorce, Mitchell left Detroit and moved to New York City, where she became part of the Greenwich Village folk scene and performed along the East Coast. By 1968, Mitchell moved to Los Angeles, settling in Laurel Canyon, which was becoming a hub for singer-songwriters including David Crosby, Graham Nash and others. In the mid-1970s, Mitchell moved to LA's Bel Air neighborhood, where she lived in a historic 1920s home for decades. Mitchell built her legendary music career while living in California, where she recorded many of her most acclaimed albums, including "Blue," "Court and Spark" and "Ladies of the Canyon." Mitchell has won 11 Grammy Awards and was inducted into both the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 1997. She was also recognized with the Kennedy Center Honors in 2021 and received the prestigious Library of Congress Gershwin Prize for Popular Song in 2023. The musician lives in Santa Barbara, California. Mitchell is an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump and expressed frustration that she couldn't vote in U.S. elections because she was Canadian. CHRIS ROBINSON, BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN FACE BACKLASH AS 'AMERICANS HAVE HAD ENOUGH' OF BEING LECTURED: EXPERT During a performance at the Hollywood Bowl in LA in October 2024, Mitchell slammed Trump while performing her 1985 song "Dog Eat Dog," according to Billboard. After singing a lyric about wealthy financiers, she added, "Like Donald Trump!" Following her performance of the song, Mitchell responded to an audience member who shouted an anti-Trump remark. "'F--- Donald Trump.' I love that song," she said, apparently referencing rapper YG's 2016 protest song "FDT (F--- Donald Trump)" featuring the late rapper and activist Nipsey Hussle. She then encouraged Americans to participate in the 2024 U.S. presidential election, in which Trump ran against Democratic nominee former Vice President Kamala Harris. "Everybody get out and vote. This is an important one. I wish I could vote . I'm Canadian. I'm one of those lousy immigrants," Mitchell said. Months before becoming an American citizen, Mitchell criticized the political climate in the U.S. while accepting a lifetime achievement award at Canada's Juno Awards in March. At the ceremony, Mitchell praised Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, saying, "I'm so glad to be back in Canada. This man is a blessing. You guys are so fortunate." articles.summary: Vishal Chaturvedi’s 'Hanuman Ansh' has grossed Rs 439.98 cr worldwide after 69 days in theatres.
articles.body: Vishal Chaturvedi’s 'Hanuman Ansh' has grossed Rs 439.98 cr worldwide after 69 days in theatres. According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs 1.25 cr in India on Wednesday, October 14. Its total domestic net collection has reached Rs 338.33 cr, while the India gross stands at Rs 399.28 cr. Overseas earnings have contributed Rs 40.70 cr to the worldwide total.The film collected Rs 10 lakhs from overseas markets on Day 69. Its latest domestic net earnings are down 7.4% from Tuesday’s collection of Rs 1.35 cr. The film played across 2,933 shows in India, with its Hindi and Telugu versions contributing to the day’s earnings.Hanuman Ansh Day 69 Hindi and Telugu collectionsThe Hindi version of 'Hanuman Ansh' collected Rs 45 lakhs across 1,823 shows on Wednesday. Its overall occupancy stood at 10%. The Telugu version earned Rs 80 lakhs from 1,110 shows, registering an occupancy of 19%.The Hindi release arrived in theatres on August 7, 2026, while the Telugu version was released on October 9. Wednesday marked Day 69 for the Hindi version and Day 6 for the Telugu release. Together, the two versions earned Rs 1.25 cr in domestic net collections.Hanuman Ansh weekly box office breakdownAccording to Sacnilk, the film collected Rs 1.08 cr during its first week, followed by Rs 40 lakhs in the second week. The third-week collection rose to Rs 10.40 cr, before earnings reached Rs 61 cr in Week 4.The film recorded its highest weekly collections during the fifth and sixth weeks, earning Rs 90.25 cr and Rs 80.25 cr, respectively. articles.title: La principal revista de cine de EEUU dedica la portada a 'La bola negra' y dicta sentencia: "Podría ganar el primer Óscar para Netflix"
articles.standfirst: 'Variety' ha hablado con los dos actores Guitarricadelafuente y Miguel Bernardeau antes de su estreno en Estados Unidos
articles.summary: 'Variety' ha hablado con los dos actores Guitarricadelafuente y Miguel Bernardeau antes de su estreno en Estados Unidos
articles.body: La aclamada película 'La Bola Negra', dirigida por Los Javis, se ha convertido en el fenómeno cinematográfico de la temporada y apunta directamente a los premios de la Academia a horas de su estreno en Estados Unidos cuando las salas la proyecten el 16 de octubre. Una película que no ha pasado inadvertida para la revista 'Variety', una de las principales especializadas en cine en el país yankee, que han entrevistado y dedicado su portada de esta semana al film con Miguel Bernardeau y el cantante Guitarricadelafuente. Al estar ambientada en un momento muy concreto de la historia de España, han tenido que explicar lo que sucedió en la Guerra Civil y que para ellos no era ninguna novedad: "Es algo que nos ha afectado a todos; nuestros bisabuelos estuvieron involucrados. Es algo común en la sociedad española", dice Guitarricadelafuente. Una película con una historia novedosa en Estados Unidos que si consigue cumplir algunos pronósticos avanzan que será un éxito para Netflix: "Si la película triunfa en los Premios de la Academia, será un hito para el cine mundial, para Netflix y para los artistas queer", escriben en 'Variety'. Una cinta que, según describen, entrelaza el romance, la memoria histórica de España y la identidad queer a través de varias líneas temporales. Todo tras publicar un reportaje con sus protagonistas que reconocen que su mayor reto no fue la química en pantalla. "No fue difícil enamorarme de él", confiesa Guitarricadelafuente. Los actores explican que se sometieron a una rigurosa preparación para encarnar a un prisionero de guerra y su custodio en 1937: "Recibimos entrenamiento militar: cómo sujetar un fusil", señala el de Benicassim sobre el rodaje. La película que también contó con personalidades más conocidas en Hollywood como Penélope Cruz o Glenn Close, llega haciendo gala de esa dulzura y autenticidad que han cautivado ya la crítica internacional desde su paso por Cannes y el Festival de Toronto, posicionando a la producción como una de las grandes favoritas del año, incluso para los Premios Oscar y que hasta la revista se atreve a hacer un pronóstico en el titular del reportaje: "Sexo, amor y guerra: cómo la atrevida epopeya gay 'La Bola Negra' podría ganar el primer Óscar a la Mejor Película para Netflix". Con el respaldo de Netflix y un estreno comercial cuidadosamente planificado, el equipo de "La Bola Negra" afronta la carrera hacia los Óscar con prudencia pero con una enorme ilusión. La película se estrenará en Estados Unidos el próximo 16 de octubre y Netflix la mantendrá en salas durante 47 días en el país norteamericano. Una confianza que tildan que es "sin precedentes". Un acuerdo que llegó el último día de festival, dicen, pero que llega a tiempo para soñar con el éxito en Estados Unidos y, por qué no, con el reconocimiento de 'Hollywood'.

articles.title: Vicente Vallés, periodista, señala a las autoridades españolas y marroquíes por la invasión en Ceuta: "Eran conscientes y no se hizo nada"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de ‘Antena 3 Noticias’ cree que hubo que tomar otras decisiones
articles.summary: El presentador de ‘Antena 3 Noticias’ cree que hubo que tomar otras decisiones
articles.body: Han pasado más de dos meses desde la invasión a Ceuta y la ciudad autónoma continúa pidiendo medios para salir de esta situación. En ‘La Mesa’ de Antena 3 han contado con Vicente Vallés. El periodista de esta casa considera que las autoridades marroquíes y las españolas estaban al tanto de lo que estaba ocurriendo, solo que no hicieron nada para remediarlo. El comunicador se basa en una idea: es imposible movilizar a tantas personas hacia la frontera de otro país sin que ninguno de los dos fuese consciente de lo que estaba ocurriendo. “El conocimiento básico que podemos tener de lo que se publicó hace pensar que, lógicamente, sí hubo una implicación de las autoridades marroquíes”. “Es muy difícil imaginar que 80.000 personas puedan llegar a Castillejos y de Castillejos atravesar la frontera para España sin que nadie se entere de que eso se está produciendo”, sentencia el presentador de Atresmedia. De hecho, en uno de los informes del CNI queda constancia, el día 29, de que también se había avisado a Marruecos de lo que estaba a punto de suceder. “No se hizo nada o nada sustancial para evitarlo. Pero no solo en Marruecos, tampoco las autoridades españolas hicieron nada para proteger la frontera el día 30 y 31”, zanja Vallés sobre la implicación de ambas naciones. A 15 de octubre, las labores de identificación en la ciudad autónoma ceutí continúan. No obstante, los vecinos denuncian que muchos migrantes han huido para no pasar por este trámite. Sin ir más lejos, en ‘La Mesa’ también estuvo Melchor León, diputado del PSOE en Ceuta, que explicó su intención de no votar a Pedro Sánchez el 29-N: “Por la nefasta gestión que ha hecho de la grave invasión que sufrimos en Ceuta”.

articles.title: Dabiz Muñoz, chef: "Freír un huevo es fácil, freírlo bien no es tan fácil"
articles.standfirst: Explica cómo conseguir un huevo frito con la clara crujiente, la tradicional puntilla dorada y la yema cremosa utilizando aceite de oliva muy caliente
articles.summary: Explica cómo conseguir un huevo frito con la clara crujiente, la tradicional puntilla dorada y la yema cremosa utilizando aceite de oliva muy caliente
articles.body: El huevo frito es uno de los platos más sencillos de la cocina doméstica, pero conseguir que la clara quede en su punto y que los bordes estén crujientes mientras la yema mantiene una textura cremosa requiere prestar atención a varios detalles. Dabiz Muñoz, chef madrileño al frente de DiverXO, ha compartido en sus redes sociales su particular método para preparar esta elaboración, con una premisa clara: la temperatura del aceite y la textura final son fundamentales. El cocinero, que cuenta con tres estrellas Michelin en DiverXO, explicó su técnica en una publicación de Instagram que recuperaron distintos medios gastronómicos. Su propuesta se basa en utilizar abundante aceite de oliva muy caliente y conseguir una clara con una puntilla bien tostada, sin que el resto del huevo quede demasiado hecho. "Me flipan los huevos fritos en mucho aceite de oliva humeante, con la puntilla bien tostada y muy crujiente, el resto de la clara no muy hecha y la yema cocinada, pero cremosa, que no líquida", explicó el chef. La primera clave está en calentar una cantidad generosa de aceite de oliva virgen extra en una sartén. Muñoz recomienda que alcance una temperatura elevada, hasta el punto de humear, antes de incorporar el huevo. La idea es que el calor permita que los bordes de la clara se doren rápidamente y desarrollen esa textura crujiente que caracteriza a los huevos fritos con puntilla. El segundo aspecto importante es no manipular demasiado el huevo durante la fritura. Una vez incorporado al aceite, hay que dejar que la clara vaya cuajando y que los bordes adquieran el color dorado deseado. Según la técnica que muestra el cocinero, se puede utilizar una espumadera para recoger parte del aceite caliente y echarlo con cuidado sobre la clara, ayudando a terminar su cocción sin tener que darle la vuelta al huevo. El objetivo es encontrar el equilibrio entre las diferentes texturas: una puntilla crujiente, una clara hecha pero todavía jugosa y una yema cremosa. Para Muñoz, este último punto es especialmente importante, ya que no busca una yema completamente líquida, sino una textura más densa.

articles.title: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle accused of staging 'royal theatre' as King Charles faces new dilemma: expert
articles.summary: Royal experts say the Sussexes' Nottingham charity visit risks defying Queen Elizabeth II's rule against a "half in, half out" arrangement.
articles.body: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are being accused of playing royals on their own terms — and sidestepping the late Queen Elizabeth II's wishes in the process. On Oct. 15, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex are scheduled to visit Nottingham for their first joint public appearance since returning to the U.K., Fox News Digital confirmed. The city holds special significance for the couple, as it was the first place they visited after announcing their engagement in November 2017. Kinsey Schofield, host of the YouTube show "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital that, based on her sources, "there is frustration" inside Buckingham Palace as Harry and Meghan prepare to visit several charities in a manner resembling an official royal engagement. KING CHARLES DRAWS ‘LINE IN THE SAND’ WITH PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE AFTER COUPLE CAUGHT OFF GUARD: EXPERT "Harry and Meghan are no longer working members of the royal family," Schofield said. "King Charles recently reminded his government that the Sussexes are private citizens. The Sussexes appear increasingly determined to recreate the optics of royal life without the responsibilities that come with it. … The charitable visits, the appearances, the photographers. It’s royal theatre without royal authority." "Royal engagements aren't just photo-ops," Schofield said. "There's diplomacy involved. There's soft power. Working royals represent the sovereign, strengthen relationships and serve the interests of the country. Harry and Meghan appear more interested in faking the image of royalty than embracing its purpose. They can imitate the engagement, but they can't replicate the authority or constitutional significance." "They are pushing to reclaim the spotlight they left behind," British broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "It's definitely a reboot — a pseudo royal reboot." WATCH: PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE CAUSED QUEEN STRESS IN FINAL YEARS: AUTHOR In January 2020, Queen Elizabeth II drew a firm line at the Sandringham Summit: There would be no "half in, half out" role for the Sussexes. They couldn't remain working members of the royal family while pursuing independent, income-generating ventures. The couple stepped back from royal duties that year, citing intrusive coverage by the British press and a lack of support from the palace. "Following conversations with the duke, the queen has written confirming that in stepping away from the work of the royal family it is not possible to continue with the responsibilities and duties that come with a life of public service," Buckingham Palace said in a statement on Feb. 19, 2021. In response, the couple issued a statement of their own, saying: "We can all live a life of service. Service is universal." In Nottingham, the couple will focus on charitable work. articles.body: The Supreme Court has allowed actor Rajpal Yadav to seek the release of his passport so he can travel to Canada for a film shoot, even as his cheque-bounce case continues. The court also sent his money dispute with creditors to mediation.Passport release with conditionsThe court said the passport can be released “subject to conditions” set by the trial court. Rajpal Yadav must follow these conditions before he travels abroad.As per a LiveLaw report, advocate Vikrant Yadav, who appeared for the actor, asked for the passport to be released. He told the court that the actor might need to travel overseas for work.The court also directed that Rajpal Yadav must inform the trial court once he returns from his trip.Dispute sent to mediationThe bench observed that the matter was fit for an amicable settlement through mediation, considering the issues raised and the complexity involved. A mediator has been appointed, and both sides have been asked to contact the mediator and fix a date. The mediator may ask them to appear in person or online.The court noted that Rs 2 crore has already been deposited with its registry. The mediation is expected to address the pending money issues between the actor and his creditors. Meanwhile, the passport order will let him continue with his professional commitments, subject to the trial court’s conditions.What is the Rajpal Yadav cheque-bounce case?The case goes back to 2010, when Yadav took Rs 5 crore from Murali Projects Pvt Ltd to fund his film ‘Ata Pata Laapata’, his first as director. The film did not do well at the box office and led to heavy losses. Under a later settlement, Yadav, his wife and their company reportedly agreed to repay the amount with interest.In 2013, the actor gave seven cheques of Rs 1.05 crore each towards repayment, but all of them bounced. This led to seven cheque-bounce cases against him.Rajpal Yadav spoke of his strugglesEarlier this month, Rajpal Yadav appeared before the Supreme Court and spoke about the financial and professional troubles he faced during the long legal fight. He claimed ‘Ata Pata Laapata’ caused him a loss of Rs 17 crore and that the case hurt his career and reputation.At the October 7 hearing, he also said he had thought of the title ‘Solah Sawan Jhel Ke’ for a film based on his own experiences.
